name: Suez Canal
hook: De Lesseps, Disraeli's shares and Nasser's seizure — the shortcut that keeps becoming a crisis.

facts.statement: Completed in 1869 and nicknamed "the Highway to India," the canal has no locks because the Mediterranean and the Red Sea sit at nearly the same level.

facts.label: Ferdinand de Lesseps
facts.statement: French diplomat Ferdinand de Lesseps promoted and built the Suez Canal, then failed at Panama.

facts.label: Port Said
facts.statement: Port Said, founded when construction began in 1859, stands where the canal meets the Mediterranean.

facts.label: Gamal Abdel Nasser
facts.statement: Nasser nationalized the canal on July 26, 1956, to collect tolls for the Aswan Dam, setting off the Suez Crisis.

facts.label: the Rothschilds
facts.statement: In 1875 the Rothschilds floated the loan that let Britain buy Egypt's shares in the canal.

facts.label: the Sinai Peninsula
facts.statement: The canal separates the Sinai Peninsula — and Africa — from the rest of Asia.

facts.label: the Statue of Liberty
facts.statement: Frédéric Bartholdi first wanted his colossal statue to light the way to Asia at the Suez Canal; when that plan died, it became the Statue of Liberty in New York.
